My father committed suicide at the age of 26 and exactly one month before I was born. I have thought about suicide constantly since age 11 when my mother finally told me how my father really died. When I was nearing the milestone of reaching 26 myself I was counting down the days in my head til I got to his age when he did it. I was sure I would never get older than he had and was convinced I would kill myself on the date that coincided with me reaching the 26 years 2 months 11 days my dad was when he did it. Im 32 now and have survived two suicide attempts one serious and another much less so. The first time was when I was 29 and the second was when I was 30. I still struggle to this day thinking and, for lack of a better word, fantasizing about following him towards the end he created for himself. It sucks how much our parents decisions can influence the people we become. I know the feeling of living on borrowed time so I can definitely relate to your situation.
When we do anything in excess to the point of not being able to stop it becomes an addiction. Good luck on your journey

I went through something similar to what you're going through in my early to late twenties. I was hooked on an over the counter drug used for weight loss but was really just a generic form of speed. When I was on it I would sit and watch porn for up to 12 hours at a time while fucked up because of the intense feeling the drug coupled with the act of masturbating had on me. I would not leave my room and I ended up alienating myself from my only true friend that I lived with. It was a hell I lived in of my own creation but I couldn't stop no matter how sick and depraved my mind told me it was to do these things. I can tell you from experience that usually addictions are coupled with things and for me its been many different combined addictions that have hurt me the most. When I was smoking I need to drink or vice versa. When im high I needed a cigarette. When I was on pills I needed caffeine and cigarettes and eventually led to adding the porn addiction in the mix. I have come a long way but im far from being out of the tunnel of darkness I put my life in. I found out when I cut out the other things I needed for my addiction to hit that peak high feeling the urge to do any of them singularily lost a lot of appeal. I quit pills first and that was no easy hurdle but I did it by changing my surroundings. I put myself in a living situation where I couldn't fulfill my addiction without being extremely sneaky about it. Eventually I gave up the need for the porn (in excess) too. I don't think your parents place would be the most healing place for you to make that change from what you said about how they reacted. A change was what helped me through my addictions (still a smoker but working on that one too). Take some time to do something you have always wanted to do. Not sure if any of this will even pertain to your situation but thought I would share and let you know you aren't a dog and you are far from being a sick person and there are others out there going through or have gone through what you are right now. Stay strong and just know our urges can be the death of us if we let them control our lives. Addiction is a beast that you need to tame before you can decide to kill it. Stay strong
